sources.entry: Peer-to-peer file sharing is the distribution and sharing of digital media using peer-to-peer (P2P) networking technology.

summary.name: Peer-to-peer (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of peer-to-peer (P2P) computing and networking, where participants share their own resources directly with each other rather than through central servers.
use_cases: understanding how p2p file sharing works
researching p2p security and malware risks
summary.what_it_does: The page is an encyclopedia article describing peer-to-peer networking as a distributed architecture where participants act as both resource providers and requesters. It explains the difference between unstructured networks (flooding-based search) and structured networks (DHT-based lookup), plus hybrid models that use a central server to help peers find each other. It covers history from Usenet and ARPANET through Napster (1999), and discusses security threats such as routing attacks and malware, resilience and availability trade-offs, incentive problems like freeloading, and copyright legal cases. It also lists example P2P applications and protocols, including BitTorrent, IPFS, Syncthing, and WebTorrent.
notable: Explains unstructured vs structured vs hybrid P2P overlay designs
Covers P2P history from Usenet and ARPANET to Napster
Discusses security issues such as routing attacks and malware prevalence in P2P networks
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software product; it has no download or license information
Article notes it needs more citations
